rot.knightFork.ideia.ex1.e1: Attack: a fork is a move in which one piece attacks two enemy pieces at once. Your opponent can only save one of them.
rot.knightFork.ideia.ex1.e2: The knight is the classic forking piece: it jumps, and its attack cannot be blocked by a piece in the way.
rot.knightFork.ideia.ex1.e3: The black king is on g8 and the black queen on d7. There is a square from which the knight on d5 reaches both.
rot.knightFork.ideia.ex1.p: Find the knight jump that attacks the king and the queen.
rot.knightFork.ideia.ex1.certo: Yes, the knight on f6 makes the fork: it checks the king and, from the same square, attacks the queen on d7.
rot.knightFork.ideia.ex1.revela: The jump is to f6: from there the knight checks the king on g8 and attacks the queen on d7 at the same time.
rot.knightFork.ideia.ex1.err.d5e7.1: On e7 the knight also gives check, but from there it does not attack the queen, and the queen guards that square.
rot.knightFork.ideia.ex1.err.d5e7.2: After this move Black has a resource: the queen captures the knight on e7.
rot.knightFork.ideia.ex1.err.d5e7.3: Back to the position: look for the square that attacks the king and the queen.
rot.knightFork.ideia.ex1.fora: That move does not attack the king and the queen at once. Look for a square within reach of the knight on d5 that hits both.
rot.knightFork.ideia.ex1.volta: Try again: look for the knight jump.
rot.knightFork.ideia.ex1.l1: Because of the check, Black must deal with the king before anything else, and the queen has no time to escape.
rot.knightFork.ideia.ex1.l2: The king goes to g7, gets out of check and attacks the knight, but the knight moves first.
rot.knightFork.ideia.ex1.l3: The knight captures the queen on d7. White is left with rook and knight against the pawns.
rot.knightFork.ideia.ex1.l4: This is the strongest fork, the fork with check: the opponent has no time to save the other piece.
rot.knightFork.ideia.ex2.e1: Attack: now let us think from Black's side. A fork also works without check, against two pieces worth more than the knight or left undefended.
rot.knightFork.ideia.ex2.e2: The white queen is on e3 and the white bishop on e5. Neither one defends the other.
rot.knightFork.ideia.ex2.p: Find the jump of the knight on f6 that attacks the queen and the bishop.
rot.knightFork.ideia.ex2.certo: Yes, from g4 the knight attacks the queen on e3 and the bishop on e5 at the same time.
rot.knightFork.ideia.ex2.revela: The jump is to g4: from there the knight attacks the queen on e3 and the bishop on e5.
rot.knightFork.ideia.ex2.fora: That move does not attack the queen and the bishop at once. Look for the square from which the knight on f6 reaches e3 and e5.
rot.knightFork.ideia.ex2.volta: Try again: look for the jump of the knight on f6.
rot.knightFork.ideia.ex2.l1: White must save the queen and, if possible, the bishop too, with a single move.
rot.knightFork.ideia.ex2.l2: The queen goes to g3: it escapes, defends the bishop and even attacks the knight.
rot.knightFork.ideia.ex2.l3: The knight captures the bishop on e5 anyway: the pawn on d6 guards e5, and if the queen recaptures, the pawn captures the queen.
rot.knightFork.ideia.ex2.l4: A fork works when the opponent cannot save both pieces: either no move protects both, or the defence does not hold, like the queen that cannot recapture on e5. And the knight cannot be captured on the fork square without loss.
rot.knightFork.demos.partida.1: Attack: this position comes from a game played on Lichess. The black king is on c7 and the black queen on f6; the knight on c3 has a square that reaches both.
rot.knightFork.demos.partida.2: The knight jumps to d5: it checks the king on c7 and attacks the queen on f6.
rot.knightFork.demos.partida.3: The king goes to d7 and gets out of check, but the queen is still attacked.
rot.knightFork.demos.partida.4: The knight captures the queen on f6, again with check, now against the king on d7.
rot.knightFork.demos.partida.5: The knight from g8 recaptures on f6. White has traded a knight for the queen.
rot.knightFork.demos.f7.1: Attack: a fork can also start with a capture. Look at the black queen on d8 and the black rook on h8.
rot.knightFork.demos.f7.2: The knight captures the pawn on f7 and attacks the queen on d8 and the rook on h8. The king cannot capture the knight: the rook on f2 guards f7.
rot.knightFork.demos.f7.3: The queen goes to d5 and is safe.
rot.knightFork.demos.f7.4: The knight captures the rook on h8.
rot.knightFork.demos.excecao.1: Attack: a teaching example like the first one, but now there is a black bishop on g7.
rot.knightFork.demos.excecao.2: The jump to f6 looks like the same fork, with check to the king and an attack on the queen.
rot.knightFork.demos.excecao.3: The bishop on g7 captures the knight, because it guards f6. Here the fork does not work, and White just loses the knight.
rot.knightFork.demos.excecao.4: Back to the position: before the fork, check who guards the destination square.
rot.knightFork.demos.excecao.5: The right move here is to bring the rook to d1: it defends the knight, which the queen on d7 attacks, and the position is balanced.
rot.knightFork.pratica.ataque.enunciado: Now let us think from Black's side. Play as Black and find the best move.
rot.knightFork.pratica.ataque.fim: The knight check from f3 forced the king to move, and the knight captured the queen on g5: the fork with check won the queen.
rot.knightFork.pratica.defesa.enunciado: Defence: the black knight on d4 threatens to jump to c2, checking the king and attacking the rook on a1. Play as White and find a move that stops the fork.
rot.knightFork.pratica.defesa.fim: Before each move, check the squares the enemy knight can reach. Moving the king or the rook out of its reach, or guarding c2, defuses the fork.
rot.knightFork.pratica.defesa.err.c2c3: With 1.c3? you attack the knight, but it does not need to run: 1...Nc2+ gives check and next move captures the rook on a1.
rot.knightFork.pratica.defesa.err.f1c4: With 1.Bc4? you develop the bishop but leave the threat: 1...Nc2+ gives check and captures the rook on a1 next move.
rot.knightFork.pratica.defesa.err.f1e2: With 1.Be2? you develop the bishop but leave the threat: 1...Nc2+ gives check and captures the rook on a1 next move.
rot.knightFork.pratica.defesa.err.g5e3: With 1.Be3? you attack the knight, but it does not need to run: 1...Nc2+ gives check and next move captures the rook on a1.
rot.knightFork.pratica.valeAqui.enunciad: The knight on e5 can jump to f7 and attack both black rooks. Does the fork work here? Before deciding, look at Black's threats. Play as White and find the best move.
rot.knightFork.pratica.valeAqui.fim: Here the fork did not work. The bishop captures on g4 with check to the king on c8; when the queen recaptures, the knight on e5 captures the queen, because it guarded g4.
rot.knightFork.pratica.valeAqui.err.e5f7: With 15.Nxf7? the fork does not work: Black plays 15...Qxh1+ and captures the rook with check before saving their own.
